Revised 2026-10-19: Cuyo is not Peru's loss; it passes from the Captaincy General of Chile (Chile dossier /ledger/11; Chile page: 'The Mendoza and San Juan territories were transferred to ... the Rio de la Plata in 1776').
1796: Puno returns to Peru. 'In 1796, Puno became part of the Viceroyalty of Peru.'

region.text: the Province of Maynas, read as Loreto

ledger.note: 1802: Maynas returns to Peru. The New Granada page lists the Province of Maynas for '1739-1802' without naming a recipient; the Peru page records Requena's proposal to reincorporate it into Peru without a date.

1803: Guayaquil is placed under Peru. The New Granada page lists the Province of Guayaquil for '1763 to 1803' and does not explain the change; Peru as the recipient is the researcher's reading. Confidence 1: page silent on 1803.

region.text: Upper Peru: Chuquisaca, La Paz, Potosi, Cochabamba, Moxos and Chiquitos

ledger.note: 1810: Upper Peru is annexed to Peru. It was 'annexed by the Viceroyalty of Peru as an emergency measure to stop the spread of the revolution' (the intendancies of Chuquisaca, La Paz, Potosi, Cochabamba, plus Moxos and Chiquitos); the page gives the year of the May Revolution without a month.
1814 (3 August): a junta under Pumacahua takes Cuzco. 'Criollo leaders formed a junta under Mateo Pumacahua on 3 August 1814.'
1815: the Cuzco rebellion is crushed. 'Royal forces crushed the rebellion by mid-1815 and executed Pumacahua.'
1820: Guayaquil proclaims itself independent. 'Guayaquil proclaimed itself an independent state in 1820.' The page lists it among Peru's territorial losses.

region.text: the bay of Pisco in the Region of Ica

ledger.note: 1820 (7 September): San Martin's Liberation Expedition lands at Pisco. 'On 7 September the Liberation expedition arrived on the bay of Pisco in today's Region of Ica.' The Sierra Campaign of Arenales began on 5 October 1820 and proclaimed Huamanga's independence on 1 November.
1821: the viceroy moves the capital from Lima to Cusco. Infobox 'Capital: Lima (1535-1821); Cusco (1821-1824)'; de la Serna 'moved his headquarters to Cuzco' (Peruvian independence page).

notes:
Written by am-06-x from four pages (budget 2-5). Not settled:
(1) No page gives the viceroyalty's boundary or a boundary change between 1563 and 1717; all keyframes use Cliopatria's Spanish Empire shape inside the South American countries, minus the lands the pages date away. The infobox area 1,340,000 km2 matches modern Peru, not 'most of the Spanish Empire in South America': ratio about 0.4-0.6 to the shape, flagged in the 1542 keyframe.
(2) Chile: the Peru page says a captaincy general of Chile was 'established in 1541' and 'segregated from the Viceroyalty on 1798' (a footnote), but Chile is drawn as its own state (captaincy-general-of-chile, this batch) and left out of Peru from the start. Venezuela: the Santo Domingo states (Caracas, Cumana, Margarita) are out of the Peruvian shape throughout; the Maracaibo and Guayana states are in it only while the Audiencia of Santa Fe is Peru's (1542-1716 and 1723-1738); see (7) below.
(3) Dates differ between pages: the Peru page says New Granada's first term lasted 'until 1724' and its restoration was 'permanent in 1740'; the New Granada page's 5 November 1723 and 20 August 1739 are used (here and in the New Granada dossier). Guayaquil: Peru's 1803 gain is at confidence 1; the Peru page is silent on 1803 and on Maynas's 1802 return.
(4) 1821-1824: the patriot zone around Lima and Pisco is a researcher's reading (discs of 300 and 150 km); Trujillo/Lambayeque (northern Peru) and the Huamanga highlands, which the patriots also held at times, are not separated. Cliopatria's Republic of Peru begins in 1822.
(5) Rulers: the page gives no full viceroy list; omitted. Counterparts not in polities.csv: 'Cuzco rebellion (Pumacahua junta)' and 'Free Province of Guayaquil' (names, no dossier); 'captaincy-general-of-chile' is this batch's.

Revision of 2026-10-19 (after the adversarial review; one more page opened, the Captaincy General of Venezuela, and the Peruvian War of Independence page read again):
(6) Cuyo: the 1542, 1600, 1717, 1723 and 1739 shapes and the 1542 found no longer draw Cuyo (Mendoza, San Juan, San Luis), which the Captaincy General of Chile dossier holds until 1776; the 1776 loss no longer lists it. The Rio de la Plata dossier still names Peru as Cuyo's previous holder in its 1776 found (the page: the king gave Cevallos 'the corregimiento of Cuyo' on 1 August 1776); that dossier and Chile's /ledger/11 should read Chile -> Rio de la Plata.
(7) Venezuela: the 1542-1716 and 1723-1738 shapes drew all of Venezuela although the notes said it was out. The Captaincy General of Venezuela page puts Caracas, Cumana and Margarita under the Audiencia of Santo Domingo and only Maracaibo, Guayana and Trinidad under the Bogota audiencia (hence under Peru when Santa Fe was Peru's, 1723-1739). The shapes now drop the central, eastern and island states (Falcon, Lara, Yaracuy, Carabobo, Aragua, Miranda, Vargas, Distrito Capital, Guarico, Cojedes, Anzoategui, Monagas, Sucre, Nueva Esparta: the researcher's reading of the three provinces) and keep Zulia, Merida, Trujillo, Tachira, Barinas, Apure, Portuguesa, Bolivar, Amazonas and Delta Amacuro. The Peru page says Peru 'originally contained ... most of the Spanish Empire in South America'; where it conflicts with the Venezuela page, the Venezuela page's provincial detail is followed. The notes' sentence 'Venezuela is out of the Peruvian shape throughout (it was in New Granada, then the Venezuela captaincy general)' is replaced by this.
(8) Quito: the 1717 shape, the 1717 loss and the 1723 gain now exclude/include Ecuador's Quito as the New Granada page lists 'Quito (1717 to 1723 and 1739 to 1822)'. The 1739 loss already had Ecuador.
(9) Wars: 'Peruvian War of Independence' and the Upper Peru war now end in 1824, the year of the dissolution; Callao (Real Felipe) and Chiloe surrendered in January 1826 and Sucre's Upper Peru campaign ended in April 1825, after the dossier's end. The dossier was not extended to 1826.
(10) Areas after the subtractions: 1542-1599 2.06 M km2 (infobox 1.34 M km2, ratio 0.65), 1600-1716 and 1723-1738 3.13 M km2. Not done: the thin item on the 1563-1717 boundaries (Real Audiencia of Charcas page) was not opened; the 1600-1716 keyframe is still Cliopatria's Spanish Empire shape (3.65 M km2 before these subtractions) against the infobox's 1.34 M km2.
